habitat: Lakes, floodplains, dams and sewage ponds, including shallow fresh water with grassy edges. Numbers on seasonal waters rise after rain.
summary: A medium dabbling duck with a pinkish-red bill, a dark cap, a pale face and spotting over the body. It is larger than Blue-billed Teal, which has a blue-grey bill and an unspeckled rear body. In flight the speculum is creamy, and Wikipedia describes the secondaries as buff with a black stripe. The sexes are similar. Juveniles are duller. Sounds are soft at close range, and the female can give a louder series of quacks.

similar.note: Blue-billed Teal is much smaller, with a grey-blue bill and no speckling on the rear body. Red-billed Teal has a pinkish-red bill and spotting over the whole body.
Cape Teal also has a reddish bill, but it is paler, with a uniform head and no dark cap.

head.pattern: Wikipedia: a blackish cap and nape contrast with a pale face. The sexes are similar.

upperparts.pattern: The body is spotted. Newman says the spotting covers the body.

wings.pattern: Newman: a creamy speculum. Wikipedia: the secondaries are buff with a black stripe.

viewNotes.note: A dark cap, pale face and pinkish-red bill, with spotting along the body.
The dark cap and pale cheeks meet on the front of the head, and the red bill is obvious.
The spotted back continues the body pattern. The creamy speculum is a flight mark.
The speculum is creamy. Wikipedia adds a black stripe on the buff secondaries.
The underwing is not given a separate colour in these texts.
Wikipedia says juveniles are duller. The texts do not name which parts change.

calls.description: Wikipedia describes the male call as a whzzt.
Newman says the female may give a louder series of quacks that decrease in volume. Wikipedia calls the female sound a soft, mallard-like quack.

Most sounds are soft and audible only at close range. The catalogue cut is not labelled male or female. Grade B, South Africa. The grade A catalogue file is ND, so this grade B Eastern Cape cut is the highest playable one. The filename says the bird was swimming.

research.note: Status is resident. SABAP1 says it is largely resident and disperses to seasonal waters after rain, including long movements, so all twelve months are listed rather than a seasonal absence. Juvenile colours, chick down and the underwing are not described. The recording is grade B because the grade A file is not a playable licence.
